query: I'm researching context engineering for LLM applications — the shift from prompt engineering to context engineering. Find me the most influential posts, threads, and articles from the past 3 months about: (1) what context engineering actually means in practice — context window management, RAG vs long context, context compression, tool output management, context ordering effects; (2) Anthropic's framing of context engineering; (3) how coding agents (Cursor, Claude Code, Codex) handle context — what goes in, what gets compressed, what gets dropped; (4) practitioners sharing real techniques for managing context in production LLM apps; (5) any contrarian takes arguing context engineering is overhyped or just rebranded prompt engineering. Focus on X/Twitter, Hacker News, and engineering blogs. For each result: give me the source link, author, and the specific technique or argument they make.

content.text:
**Anthropic’s “Effective Context Engineering for AI Agents” (Sep 2025, widely discussed/referenced in 2026) is the most cited foundational framing.**[[1]](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/effective-context-engineering-for-ai-agents)[[2]](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=45418251)

- **Source**: https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/effective-context-engineering-for-ai-agents (Anthropic engineering team).
- **Key arguments/techniques**: Context engineering is the iterative curation of the optimal token set in the context window (beyond just the prompt itself), including retrieved docs, memory, tool outputs, and history. It is positioned as the natural progression from prompt engineering. Practical tactics include static files like CLAUDE.md loaded upfront; dynamic/just-in-time retrieval via tools (e.g., glob/grep instead of loading entire files); summarization/compaction of conversation history; and lightweight compaction like tool-result clearing. It emphasizes hybrid autonomy, external indexing (like file systems), and avoiding bloated context as a “silent killer” of agent reliability.[[1]](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/effective-context-engineering-for-ai-agents)

Recent X discussions frequently reference and expand on this piece (e.g., threads breaking it down into levels or linking it to agent harnesses).[[3]](https://x.com/shmidtqq/status/2071989087225954437)

**Layered engineering frameworks (prompt → context → harness → loop)** appear in influential practitioner explanations.[[4]](https://x.com/_avichawla/status/2072980277870383366)

- **Source**: Avi Chawla (@_avichawla) X thread (Jul 2026, high engagement).
- **Key arguments/techniques**: Context engineering specifically involves everything in a turn beyond the core prompt (query + retrieved docs + memory + prior turns + tool outputs). Techniques: rerank retrieved chunks for relevance; place key facts outside the “middle” of the context (where accuracy drops); summarize old turns; evict stale outputs; push large blobs to external files. This sits between prompt engineering (wording one call) and harness/loop engineering (tools, verifiers, outer loops, stop conditions).

**Coding agents and context handling** are covered in tool-specific discussions and videos.

- **Cursor-focused sources**: YouTube “Context Engineering & Coding Agents with Cursor” (Oct 2025) and Medium article on Cursor’s dynamic context discovery (Jan 2026). Cursor emphasizes *minimal* relevant context over maximal inclusion; dynamic discovery methods to surface only what’s needed; and partnerships (e.g., with Elastic) to inject live production data/logs into agents without bloating the window.[[5]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3KAI__5dUn0)[[6]](https://medium.com/@ai-labs/cursors-new-context-discovery-principles-can-transform-how-you-use-any-ai-coding-tool-d379191d4f25)[[7]](https://www.elastic.co/blog/cursor)
- **Claude Code/Anthropic**: Uses CLAUDE.md for static context + tools (glob/grep) for dynamic retrieval; summarization of history; tool-result clearing. Avoids loading full large objects.[[1]](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/effective-context-engineering-for-ai-agents)
- **Broader coding agents** (Cursor, Claude Code, Codex, Devin, etc.): Martin Fowler’s article (Feb 2026) and Cursor forum posts discuss hooks, observability, multi-agent setups, and structured context files. Common patterns include static rules/personas vs. dynamic RAG/skills loaded on demand.[[8]](https://martinfowler.com/articles/exploring-gen-ai/context-engineering-coding-agents.html)[[9]](https://forum.cursor.com/t/context-engineering-how-to-give-your-ai-agents-the-perfect-context-for-every-task/116717)

**HN discussions** provide practitioner threads and some contrarian views.

- **Key threads**: “Effective context engineering for AI agents” (HN item 45418251, strong engagement) — users discuss visualization needs, real-world exercises with smaller windows, and tooling gaps. “The new skill in AI is not prompting, it’s context engineering” (HN item 44427757, very high points/comments) links to Phil Schmid’s blog and Simon Willison’s writing; comments debate whether it’s a meaningful distinction or rebranded prompt engineering, with some calling it a buzzword while others highlight production challenges like context rot and non-uniform performance across windows.[[2]](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=45418251)[[10]](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=44427757)
- Other HN mentions cover “context rot,” compaction techniques, and how larger windows enable but don’t eliminate the need for engineering.[[11]](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=44564248)

**Practitioner techniques in production** appear in blogs, X shares, and tool integrations.

- Elastic blog (Apr 2026) on Cursor partnership: Injects operational data (logs, alerts) via native plugins for grounded agent actions.[[7]](https://www.elastic.co/blog/cursor)
- X threads and posts (e.g., @Av1dlive, @Pavan_Belagatti) share structured approaches: global/project context + memory + task files + success criteria; static (always-loaded rules/personas) vs. dynamic (on-demand skills/RAG); six context types (instructions, knowledge, memory, examples, tools, guardrails). Techniques include intentional compaction, external files for large data, and agent skills as portable procedural packages.[[12]](https://x.com/Av1dlive/status/2073394238554009933)[[13]](https://x.com/Pavan_Belagatti/status/2079241599515759033)
- Gergely Orosz interview with Dex (@dexhorthy, Jul 2026) covers practicals like identifying the “dumb zone” in long contexts, intentional compaction, context overload avoidance, and related concepts (harness/loop engineering).[[14]](https://x.com/GergelyOrosz/status/2077434907274428914)

**Contrarian/rebranded takes** are mostly in comment sections rather than dedicated posts.

- HN threads explicitly question the term (“just rebranded prompt engineering,” “buzzword,” or “the work matters more than the name”), noting overlap with existing practices while acknowledging production-scale needs like curation and rot management.[[10]](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=44427757)
- Some X posts frame context engineering as an evolution or “commodity shift” from prompts, but few strong “overhyped” standalone threads in the recent results; skepticism tends to appear as replies emphasizing that clever prompts still matter or that it’s mostly system/harness work.[[15]](https://x.com/tonsofpetefun/status/2080670439307981074)

These results focus on the most referenced and recent (post-Apr 2026) material from the specified sources. Anthropic’s piece and layered-framework explanations dominate influence, with concrete techniques centered on dynamic loading, compaction/summarization, minimalism, and separation of static/dynamic context. For deeper dives, start with the Anthropic article and the high-engagement X/HN threads linked above.
